paragraphs: Gameweek 6 flipped the table on its head. **Ahuja** produced the week's best score, 72, to leap from 5th to 1st, with O'Shea's 11 (an auto-sub for the non-playing Szoboszlai) and Verbruggen's 9 both picks no one else counted. **Klotz** climbed from 4th to joint second on 67, led by unique returns from Dewsbury-Hall (13) and Cunha (10). The fallers were **Wedd**, who dropped from 1st to 4th with 39, his lowest of the season after captain Isak and Watkins both played 0 minutes, and **Shao**, who slid from 3rd to last after taking the league's first transfer hit of the season, 4 points for two moves, and scoring 47.

**Ahuja** now leads on 367, four ahead of **Klotz** and **Croft**, who are level on 363, and just 20 points separate first from last. João Pedro, missing a week earlier, returned 12 for all four managers who owned him, and Haaland's 6 became 12 for the four who captained him. **Shao** owned Haaland but captained Saka (2 points, 4 doubled), and the armband on Haaland instead would have been worth four more points. **Croft** left 22 points on his bench, 13 of them from Dewsbury-Hall, who returned 13 in **Klotz**'s XI, while **Mariswamy** moved up to 5th on 348, helped by a unique 9 from Calafiori.
